body: this is essentially a duplicate of #6253.   as noted, you should do query(First).select_from(First).join(...) to do what you need.       unlike #6253 though there at least is a chance this can be improved by storing the "joinpoint" along with the join info when join() is called, so I will add this to our current list but long term I see Query and with_entities overall as legacy.
this is an exact dupblicate of #6089, in that case I just closed it.

It's about [Key Behavioral Changes - ORM](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/14/changelog/migration_13.html#key-behavioral-changes-orm), new in 1.4.

My query works fine in 1.3 and has the ON clause, though it's multiple ones and hence are wrapped with `_and` function.

```python
db_session.query(HomozygousVariant, Variant)
        .filter(HomozygousVariant.individual == individual.phenopolis_id)
        .join(
            Variant,
            and_(
                HomozygousVariant.CHROM == Variant.CHROM,
                HomozygousVariant.POS == Variant.POS,
                HomozygousVariant.REF == Variant.REF,
                HomozygousVariant.ALT == Variant.ALT,
            ),
        )
        .with_entities(Variant)
```

body: Great, thanks for responding so promptly!

Also trying to upgrade from 1.3 to 1.4 and many of our tests are failing due to this issue.

Is this expected to resolve any time soon?

it's on the short list for sure as I've formulated a way to work it out, it's more than a one-liner though.

are your issues related to either eager load options and/or .join()?  those are the two areas of functionality that I seek to add explicit structures for.
It's related to the join - exactly similar issue as reported in this ticket - where an extra table gets added in the FROM clause

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**memoize current options and joins w with_entities/with_only_cols** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2871

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
Very similar to #6052 (which is supposedly fixed?), applying any loader option breaks `with_entities()`.

**Expected behavior**
No error, this output from the test script:

```
normal
[<Thing 1>]
with entities + noload
[(1,)]
with entities + joinedload
[(1,)]
```

**To Reproduce**

```py
from sqlalchemy import *
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base  # to test on 1.3
from sqlalchemy.orm import *


Base = declarative_base()


class Thing(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'things'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    owner_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=True, index=True)
    owner = relationship('User', backref='things')

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Thing {self.id}>'


class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'users'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.id}>'


e = create_engine('postgresql:///test', echo=False)
Base.metadata.create_all(e)
s = Session(e)

if not s.query(Thing).count():
    thing = Thing(owner=User())
    s.add(thing)
    s.commit()


print('normal')
print(s.query(Thing).all())
print('with entities + noload')  # fails
print(s.query(Thing).options(noload('owner')).with_entities(Thing.id).all())
print('with entities + joinedload')  # fails
print(s.query(Thing).options(joinedload('owner')).with_entities(Thing.id).all())
```
